newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London fluctuated within narrow ranges without showing any clear direction. Near March lost $0.30 to close at $311.70 while May gave up $0.10 to close at $310.50. There was talk that Iraq had concluded a deal to buy between 4 and 6 cargoes of European refined white sugar under the UN oil-for-food deal. In New York raw sugar futures ended narrowly mixed after early on fund buying continued to bid the market higher. But buying enthusiasm logged after nearby March remained below Friday's peak of 11.12 cents/lb. March ended 1 point lower to close at 11.07 cents/lb, while May added 3 points to close at 11.10 cents/lb. The outer months ended 2 to 4 points higher. There was no fresh news to give the market direction.

HONG KONG - Sugar imports in October 1996 amounted to 22,063 tonnes, raw value, up on last year's 18,875 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1996 (January/October) up to 209,375 tonnes compared to 199,670 tonnes in the like period the previous year. Total imports in 1995 reached 237,332 tonnes, up from 208,640 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of origin in January/October 1996 were South Korea with 104,909 tonnes whites against 98,264 tonnes, Australia with 25,023 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 25,347 tonnes and China with 19,294 tonnes, up from 16,370 tonnes. Sugar exports in October 1996 were 5,501 tonnes which brought cumulative exports in January/October 1996 up to 60,315 tonnes compared to 49,184 tonnes in 1995. Total exports in 1995 reached 67,970 tonnes compared to 42,696 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in January/October 1996 were China with 41,335 tonnes whites against 24,131 tonnes and the Philippines with 5,200 tonnes raws against nil.

FRANCE - Sugar imports in October 1996, the first month of the 1996/97 campaign (October/September), amounted to 49,561 tonnes against 35,970 tonnes, raw value, in October 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 were 476,619 tonnes up from 364,140 tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October 1996 were Swaziland with 26,000 tonnes raws against 25,868 tonnes and Guadeloupe with 10,973 tonnes against nil. Sugar exports in October 1996 reached 291,854 tonnes, down from 348,480 tonnes exported in October 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 were 2.891 million tonnes against 3.067 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of destination in October 1996 were Belgium/Luxembourg with 68,174 tonnes whites against 109,635 tonnes, Saudi Arabia with 27,482 tonnes, up from 18,001 tonnes and Algeria with 26,010 tonnes compared to 39,152 tonnes.
